title: Training, Adapting, and Choosing Embedders: Visual Guide
outline: Title: Training, Adapting, and Choosing Embedders: Visual Guide

1. From Index To Model | a two-sided lever board — efSearch, nprobe and product quantization from IR 201/03 on one side, the contrastive objective, Matryoshka truncation and scalar/binary quantization on the other — each tapped for who owns it and what it moves | an embedding index only ever agrees with the embedder, so no index dial recovers a distinction the training objective never taught

2. Softmax Over Candidates | sliders for a competing document's score and the softmax temperature, recomputing each candidate's probability, p+, the loss and the gradient from the worked logits [3, 1, 0] | the contrastive loss is cross-entropy over candidates so it scores everything relatively — swap the negative at 1 for a hard one at 2.8 and p+ falls 0.844 to 0.535 while the loss rises 0.17 to 0.625

3. The Batch Is The Negatives | a batch-size slider from 4 to 128 with toggles for a mined hard negative and a duplicate intent, showing negatives per query, negative pairs per matmul, p+, loss and how much of the negative probability mass the hardest candidate holds | in-batch negatives are free but go stale as the model improves, one mined negative can carry almost the whole gradient, and a duplicate intent turns a valid passage into a negative with nothing to report it

4. Fine-Tune Or Shortlist | three modes — a fine-tune scorecard blended against a multilingual traffic slider, a model shortlist of A (0.86 at 768d) against B (0.85 at 384d) under a movable quality floor, and an instruction-prefix toggle drawn as query and passage vectors in the space | judge a fine-tune on segments and traffic mix rather than the overall two-point gain, let the floor rather than the leaderboard pick the model, and follow the model card's prefixes exactly because omitting one fails silently

5. Cheaper Vectors | a Matryoshka dimension slider (768/384/256/128) crossed with float32, int8 and binary precision, computing bytes per vector, GB for ten million vectors and the measured recall — plus an int8 bin-width calculator over [-1, 1] | truncation and quantization are different economies that compound their errors, so every configuration is measured rather than multiplied on paper, and unmeasured combinations are declared unknown instead of interpolated
